'''Virtual Modern''' — [[Blizzard Scout 1 (V)]] (200_140) |sources=* [https://web.archive.org/web/20081225225012/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/index.html Star Wars CCG cardlists index] at Decipher.com (archive, 25 December 2008) * [https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Complete Card List] (Decipher PDF, archive 28 September 2007) — Dark Vehicle: Blizzard Scout 1, Hoth, R1 * Printed face: [http://web.archive.org/web/20020327115743/http://decipher.com:80/starwars/cardlists/hoth/dark/images/blizzardscout1.gif Decipher.com card image] (Wayback copy of decipher.com/starwars/cardlists) |strategy=By Erik A. Petersenhttps://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/hoth/dark/small/blizzardscout1.html My favorite Dark Card. Enough said. Well, that would not make much of a card extra, would it? What combat vehicle is a staple of nearly every dark deck: the "Chicken Walker"! Take a look at the finalists decks from the 1997 World Championships, the mighty [[Blizzard Scout 1]] makes an appearance in both decks. Let's dissect this beauty. The [[Blizzard Scout 1]] is the AT-ST which made an extremely brief sprint across the screen during the Empire Strikes Back. What they didn't tell you in the movie was that [[Darth Vader]] was being whisked to the Echo [[Cloud City: East Platform (Docking Bay){{!}}Docking Bay]], and, by the way, he trampled [[Major Bren Derlin]] on his way in to the hangar (Sorry Mr. Claven) [You see, [[Major Bren Derlin]] was talking to [[2-1B (Too-Onebee){{!}}2-1B]] about this snowman who was the spitting image of Richard Nixon.... TRAMPLE]. [[Blizzard Scout 1]] is the prototype of the Imperial's AT-ST cards which will come in Return of the Jedi expansions. This unique walker boasts everything you look for in a card. The Chicken Walker (named as such for its awkward look) is a natural in the mountains of [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] ([[Hoth: Mountains (6th Marker){{!}}Hoth: Mountains]], the [[Hoth: Mountains (6th Marker){{!}}6th Marker]]), where it deploys for 2 and has power 4, a great ratio. But wait, let's take a very typical game situation, [[Darth Vader]] is at the Defensive Perimeter waving his lightsaber at [[Commander Luke Skywalker]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi{{!}}Obi-Wan]] and Captain [[Han Solo{{!}}Han]]. Although they are out of sagacious gifts from the mentor or witty comments about not getting cocky (see the chicken theme), they decide to pick on our poor Dark Lord and initiate a battle. Well, Mr. [[Grand Moff Tarkin{{!}}Tarkin]] just hops aboard his [[Blizzard Scout 1]] and reacts all the way over to join his comrade in arms. This interlude brings up the real benefits of [[Blizzard Scout 1]]. First, it boasts a landspeed of 3, the ability to react, a permanent pilot and a slot to fill with a pilot -- a great package deal. Remember there are several 3 ability Dark Side Pilots out there. Second, just look at that destiny, a 4! Perfect to keep your average destiny up, and pulling one of these as destiny for [[Trample]] will squash all of those pesky Light Side spies. (OK OK, if Obi, [[Luke Skywalker{{!}}Luke]], [[Princess Leia]], [[BoShek]] or [[Yoda]] pull off [[Plastoid Armor]] and get [[Undercover (Dark){{!}}Undercover]] it will miss, but don't get technical with me!) Third, the walker is forfeit 5, a great way to soak up damage (just remember to lose the pilot first). Finally, there is also an S-comp link for good measure. Drawbacks. That is a tough one with the mighty Chicken Walker. But there are a couple. This walker does not have any immunity to attrition, despite its 4 armor rating. The other drawback is more of a reminder, [[Blizzard Scout 1]] does not count towards [[Walker Garrison]] as it is not an AT-AT. Forget that arrogant [[General Veers]] in his hulking [[Blizzard 1]], live life on the edge, blaze across the [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] tundra in search of rebels to trample under foot with the all-powerful Chicken Waaaaalker! CARD COMBOS: [[Blizzard Scout 1]] + [[Admiral Motti]] + Snowtroopers (at other locations) = Keep your leader on the move to respond to battles. [[Blizzard Scout 1]] + [[Trample]] = Rebel Spies in the Lost Pile. [[Blizzard Scout 1]] + [[Boba Fett]] + [[Trample]] vs. [[Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca]] = Blizzard Scout 1 + [[Boba Fett]] vs. [[Han Solo]] (could have saved the imperials a lot on bribing [[Lando Calrissian (Dark){{!}}Lando Calrissian]]). [[Blizzard Scout 1]] + [[Tatooine (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Tatooine]] Sites = With the vast number of [[Tatooine (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Tatooine]] Sites, [[Blizzard Scout 1]] is your all-purpose scout combat vehicle! |combos=* [[Blizzard Scout 1]] + [[Admiral Motti]] + Snowtroopers (at other locations).[https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Blizzard%20Scout%201 Scomp: Blizzard Scout 1]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). Petersen My favorite Dark Card. Enough said. Well, that would not make much of a card extra, would it? What combat vehicle is a staple of nearly every dark deck: the "Chicken Walker"! Take a look at the finalists decks from the 1997 World Championships, the mighty [[Blizzard Scout 1]] makes an appearance in both decks. Let's dissect this beauty. The [[Blizzard Scout 1]] is the AT-ST which made an extremely brief sprint across the screen during the Empire Strikes Back. What they didn't tell you in the movie was that [[Darth Vader]] was being whisked to the Echo [[Cloud City: East Platform (Docking Bay){{!}}Docking Bay]], and, by the way, he trampled [[Major Bren Derlin]] on his way in to the hangar (Sorry Mr. Claven) [You see, [[Major Bren Derlin]] was talking to [[2-1B (Too-Onebee){{!}}2-1B]] about this snowman who was the spitting image of Richard Nixon.... TRAMPLE]. [[Blizzard Scout 1]] is the prototype of the Imperial's AT-ST cards which will come in Return of the Jedi expansions. This unique walker boasts everything you look for in a card. The Chicken Walker (named as such for its awkward look) is a natural in the mountains of [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] ([[Hoth: Mountains (6th Marker){{!}}Hoth: Mountains]], the [[Hoth: Mountains (6th Marker){{!}}6th Marker]]), where it deploys for 2 and has power 4, a great ratio. But wait, let's take a very typical game situation, [[Darth Vader]] is at the Defensive Perimeter waving his lightsaber at [[Commander Luke Skywalker]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi{{!}}Obi-Wan]] and Captain [[Han Solo{{!}}Han]]. Although they are out of sagacious gifts from the mentor or witty comments about not getting cocky (see the chicken theme), they decide to pick on our poor Dark Lord and initiate a battle. Well, Mr. [[Grand Moff Tarkin{{!}}Tarkin]] just hops aboard his [[Blizzard Scout 1]] and reacts all the way over to join his comrade in arms. This interlude brings up the real benefits of [[Blizzard Scout 1]]. First, it boasts a landspeed of 3, the ability to react, a permanent pilot and a slot to fill with a pilot -- a great package deal. Remember there are several 3 ability Dark Side Pilots out there. Second, just look at that destiny, a 4! Perfect to keep your average destiny up, and pulling one of these as destiny for [[Trample]] will squash all of those pesky Light Side spies. (OK OK, if Obi, [[Luke Skywalker{{!}}Luke]], [[Princess Leia]], [[BoShek]] or [[Yoda]] pull off [[Plastoid Armor]] and get [[Undercover (Dark){{!}}Undercover]] it will miss, but don't get technical with me!) Third, the walker is forfeit 5, a great way to soak up damage (just remember to lose the pilot first). Finally, there is also an S-comp link for good measure. Drawbacks. That is a tough one with the mighty Chicken Walker. But there are a couple. This walker does not have any immunity to attrition, despite its 4 armor rating. The other drawback is more of a reminder, [[Blizzard Scout 1]] does not count towards [[Walker Garrison]] as it is not an AT-AT. Forget that arrogant [[General Veers]] in his hulking [[Blizzard 1]], live life on the edge, blaze across the [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] tundra in search of rebels to trample under foot with the all-powerful Chicken Waaaaalker! CARD COMBOS: [[Blizzard Scout 1]] + [[Admiral Motti]] + Snowtroopers (at other locations) = Keep your leader on the move to respond to battles. [[Blizzard Scout 1]] + [[Trample]] = Rebel Spies in the Lost Pile. [[Blizzard Scout 1]] + [[Boba Fett]] + [[Trample]] vs. [[Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca]] = Blizzard Scout 1 + [[Boba Fett]] vs. [[Han Solo]] (could have saved the imperials a lot on bribing [[Lando Calrissian (Dark){{!}}Lando Calrissian]]). [[Blizzard Scout 1]] + [[Tatooine (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Tatooine]] Sites = With the vast number of [[Tatooine (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Tatooine]] Sites, [[Blizzard Scout 1]] is your all-purpose scout combat vehicle! |combos=* [[Blizzard Scout 1]] + [[Admiral Motti]] + Snowtroopers (at other locations). * [[Blizzard Scout 1]] + [[Trample]] [[Trample]] opponent's undercover spies. * [[Battle Deployment]] * [[Veers (V)]] |also_known_as=* Chicken Walker }}

The Master List (Dark Side p. 34)[[Media:Virtual_Legacy_Final_Master_DS.pdf|Players Committee Virtual Cards Master List (Dark Side)]], cover "official text as of April 27, 2013" (PDF built February 2014). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20170704232650/http://www.starwarsccg.org/Resources/MasterDS.pdf#page=34 Internet Archive] reprints it character for character; under the ruling of 11 November 2026 (every publication is a version), that copy is its own version, PC-E3 ([[Commence Primary Ignition (V) (Virtual Block 7) (Errata 3)]]), and the current text. The release-sheet slip prints no slip number. * '''PC-E1''' ([[Commence Primary Ignition (V) (Virtual Block 7) (Errata)]]): PC website card list, Virtual Block 7 list and Virtual master list, in every archived capture with game text, 21 July 2012 to 11 January 2013Players Committee website card list (Internet Archive captures): VBlock7Type (Virtual Block 7 list) [https://web.archive.org/web/20120721064742/http://www.starwarsccg.org/cardlists/VBlock7Type.html 21 July 2012], [https://web.archive.org/web/20121211205229/http://www.starwarsccg.org/cardlists/VBlock7Type.html 11 December 2012], [https://web.archive.org/web/20130111152155/http://www.starwarsccg.org/cardlists/VBlock7Type.html 11 January 2013]; VMasterType (Virtual master list) [https://web.archive.org/web/20120721064754/http://www.starwarsccg.org/cardlists/VMasterType.html 21 July 2012], [https://web.archive.org/web/20121211203905/http://www.starwarsccg.org/cardlists/VMasterType.html 11 December 2012], [https://web.archive.org/web/20130111135545/http://www.starwarsccg.org/cardlists/VMasterType.html 11 January 2013]. Later captures carry no game text.: “If Death Star orbits Alderaan (and [Virtual Block 7] Central Core on table), deploy on Death Star and fire Superlaser at Alderaan; it is 'blown away.' Once during your control phase, if Death Star orbiting a planet (except a Rebel Base) without related sites, may fire Superlaser at planet (regardless of Objective restrictions) as follows: Draw destiny. Add 2 if you control that system. If (destiny + Y - Z) > 8, target is 'blown away' and opponent loses 4 Force from Life Force. Y = total Death Star sites where opponent has no presence. Z = total sites at Yavin 4.” '''What changed:''' Parentheses are added around “destiny + Y - Z” (“If destiny + Y - Z > 8” becomes “If (destiny + Y - Z) > 8”). The same wording is already in the Players Committee's Holotable card data of 1 August 2010[https://github.com/ledwards/swccgvkit/blob/d14e714/db/darkside.cdf Holotable card data file, version 1 August 2010] (Players Committee data, copy on GitHub). Card data is dating evidence only, not a card document.. Icons written out in words, straight single quotes and credit lines in the list are not changes. The card list itself was generated from that Holotable data (research R7, 11 November 2026): a transcription the Players Committee published, listed because it was published. * '''PC-E2''' (this page): the Players Committee card image ([[:File:VB7-D-commenceprimaryignition-pre.gif]]) prints the original release-sheet text ([[Commence Primary Ignition (V) (Virtual Block 7)]]) again, word for word: “If Death Star orbits Alderaan (and [Virtual Block 7] Central Core on table), deploy on Death Star and fire Superlaser at Alderaan; it is 'blown away.' Once during your control phase, if Death Star orbiting a planet (except a Rebel Base) without related sites, may fire Superlaser at planet (regardless of Objective restrictions) as follows: Draw destiny. Add 2 if you control that system. If destiny + Y - Z > 8, target is 'blown away' and opponent loses 4 Force from Life Force. Y = total Death Star sites where opponent has no presence. Z = total sites at Yavin 4.” The image is dated only by its upload to the Players Committee's server: the Apache listing of the Virtual7-Dark card-image folder gives every file there the same time, 25 February 2013, 11:34Players Committee server, [https://web.archive.org/web/20190818034727/https://starwarsccg.org/cardlists/images/starwars/Virtual7-Dark/large/?C=M;O=A directory listing of cardlists/images/starwars/Virtual7-Dark/large/] sorted by date, as captured 18 August 2019 (Internet Archive). That is a bulk upload date, so the image may have been made earlier; it is placed at that date (ruling of 11 November 2026: what was uploaded last counts as the last version). It is listed as a version because it was published (ruling of 11 November 2026: every publication is a version, even a word-for-word repeat). The PC card image prints the slip number “18” at the bottom right, which the release-sheet slip does not. * '''PC-E3''' ([[Commence Primary Ignition (V) (Virtual Block 7) (Errata 3)]]): the Players Committee Virtual Cards Master List (official text as of 27 April 2013; Dark Side, p. 34) prints the original release-sheet text ([[Commence Primary Ignition (V) (Virtual Block 7)]]) again, word for word: “If Death Star orbits Alderaan (and [Virtual Block 7] Central Core on table), deploy on Death Star and fire Superlaser at Alderaan; it is 'blown away.' Once during your control phase, if Death Star orbiting a planet (except a Rebel Base) without related sites, may fire Superlaser at planet (regardless of Objective restrictions) as follows: Draw destiny. Add 2 if you control that system. If destiny + Y - Z > 8, target is 'blown away' and opponent loses 4 Force from Life Force. Y = total Death Star sites where opponent has no presence. Z = total sites at Yavin 4.” It is listed as a version because it was published (ruling of 11 November 2026: every publication is a version, even a word-for-word repeat of an earlier text), and, as the latest dated text, it is the current text. Its image is the Master List slip ([[:File:VL-history-1271-18-front-master.png]]).
